title: OBJ Trim
content: **List of Contents** **Open/Ad****d** **Arrangement** **Glue** **Set Properties** **Set Options** #### **Manage Trim as a style in the Object Browser.** **** #### #### **Open/Add** 1. Click the ![add text.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38277322074905) button in the Trim tab in the Object Browser. 2. Import an [OBJ file](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000494107-3D-File-OBJ-Import-Export#h_01J8YNPZ4XZ0BYCVRQ5PXVP1SF) as a Trim, or open the Trim (TRM) file. 3. Drag and Drop the Trim Style to the 3D window from the Object Browser. #### #### **Arrangement** You can easily place trims on the garment without gluing. 1\. Using ![Select On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38277322076313) **Select/Move** tool in the 3D toolbar , click ![Direct Positiong.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44950723624601)**Direct Positioning** next to the Gizmo. 2\. Hover over the pattern and click the desired location. #### **Selection** **Selecting trims only:** * **Single, specific trims:** Click on the trim in the 3D window with the ![Select On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38277322076313)**Select/Move** tool. Hold **Shift** to add to the selection as you click. * **Trims of the same type loaded into the scene more than once:** Select the trim group in the **Object Browser** , all instances of it will highlight in the 3D window. To select several different trim groups, hold either **Shift** or **Ctrl (Windows) / Cmmd (Mac)** to make the desired selection as you click. * **All trims present in the scene:** Right-click on any trim in the 3D window and choose **Select All Trims** from the right-click menu. **Selecting trims in combination with patterns:** 1. Select all trims needed in the **Object Browser** , all instances of them will highlight in the 3D window. 2. Hold **Shift** and add the desired patterns to the selection via the **Transform Pattern** tool in the 2D window. #### **Glue** **Single Point** 1. Click on the Trim in 3D window with ![Select On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38277322076313)**Select/Move** tool. 2. Click the Glue button next to the Gizmo, then click on the desired location. 3. Click the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38277322078617)**Simulate** tool. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38279125681945)** **Multiple Points**[**![Youtube Icon \(1\).png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53053444108825)**](https://youtu.be/iflI4v36pi4?si=UdIX4L8cmCmOnmEs&t=494) **** Attach trims to desired locations by tacking them to multiple points across various patterns. 1\. Using **![Tack On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44950723625753)Tack** tool in the 3D toolbar, click on an initial point on thr trim. 2\. Click on the desired point on the garment. _* Repeat the step to tack the trim to multiple points._ __ 3\. Click the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38277322078617)**Simulate** tool. **📝 Note:** Tack is not available on deactivated trims. #### #### **Set Properties** 1. Set the trim style properties or options by clicking the trim style in the Object Browser. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | Enter the information of trim **Specification** | **Scale** | Scale trim with X, Y, and Z-axis. **📝 Note:** You can directly scale the trim using the gizmo by clicking the ![scale_gizmo.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38277540580761)******scale** button next to the gizmo in 3D window. **Axis** | Enter the desired value for each axis. **Lock** **Aspect Ratio** | Toggle this option on to adjust a trim while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. **Weight** | Set the weight of trim. The entered value of weight is reflected in the simulation. **Material** | Set the [Material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047317454-Set-Fabric-Materials). 2. Or set the trim properties individually by clicking on the trim in 3D window. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | If each part(meshes) of the OBJ trim is composed of two or more parts, you can set the name for each part individually. **Collision** | Set whether you turn the Collision on or off. It only enables or disables the Collision of detached trim. **Collision Thickness** | Set the Collision Thickness with a garment. The higher the value is, the farther the distance with a garment is in the simulation. **Material** | Partially set the material of trim #### #### **Set Options** 1. Right- click on the trim in the 3D window to set the options. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Select All Trims** | Select all trims in the 3D Window. **Delete** | Delete selected trims. **Copy/ Paste** | Copy and paste the selected trims. **Duplicate to Symmerty Pattern** | Duplicate the selected trims to the symmetry pattern. **Unglue** | The attatched trim is being detached from the Pattern. **Hide Trim/Show All Trims** | Hide or Show all trims. **Show/Hide All Trim Stuatus Color** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48716887230233) Hide or Show the color as per its simulation status. ![Trim Simulation Status Color ON-OFF.gif](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48716887231513) ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38279125681945) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38279125683225) Simulate trim to achieve realistic movement and seamless, stable interaction with 3D garments. **📝 Note:** Trim simulation is available only for unglued trims, which are set to Activate by default with both simulation and collision applied. 1. Arrange the trim in the desired position on the 3D garment in the 3D window, then click the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38277322078617)**Simulate** tool. 2. If you want to activate only collision without simulation, right-click on the trim and click the**Freeze** menu. 3. Or, if you want to deactivate both collision and simulation, and click the **Deactivate** menu. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38279125681945)
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing and simulating trim styles within a 3D garment design environment.

title: Userpool Settings
content: ## **New in 2024.2** #### **List of Contents** Concept Instruction FAQ #### **Concept** #### **What is Userpool?** A Userpool is a list of Members authorized to use the Owner's license. The license Owner can add or delete Members' email(CLO-SET account) who are allowed to use the license. Once the Member is added to the Userpool, Members can sign in to the software using their own CLO-SET account to use the Owner's license. By doing so, the Owner no longer needs to share the license ID and password, enhancing security and collaboration efficiency. #### **Who can use Userpool?** Any users with the licenses to sign in to CLO Network Onlineauth 2024.2 and later versions. #### **Where is Userpool provided?** The Userpool and a more detailed manual are provided in License Account Admin. Below is how you can access to the Userpool Settings page. Sign in clo3d.com > Click Account( ![account_icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945712495769) ) on the top right side > Sign in ![License account admin.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945720137497) > Click ![Userpool Setting.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945720141849) on the left side #### **** #### **Instruction** #### **How to ADD members to the Userpool** **From the Userpool Settings** Click ![Add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945712513433) and type the Member's email address. For better management, you can set a Member name when adding a member. The Member will receive an invitation email with the software installer included. **From the Software (Auto Add)** If the CLO-SET account is signed in from the software, the account will be automatically added as a Member to the Userpool list. The Owner will receive the notification email when the new Member is auto added. If the Owner doesn't want the Members to be auto added, Auto Add option can be turned off. #### #### **How to DELETE members from the Userpool** Mark the Members from the list > Click ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39109913714841) Deleted Members cannot sign in to the software with their CLO-SET account to use the Owner's license. Deleted Members can be added again whenever it's needed. #### **** #### **FAQ** **Can the license Owner be the Member of the other Userpool?** Yes. If the Owner's email has the CLO-SET account and that same account is invited to another Userpool, the account can also be a Member under another Userpool. **I am invited as a Userpool Member, but cannot sign in to the software.** The Member needs to be signed up to CLO-SET and have a CLO-SET account to sign in to the software. However, any email can be added when the Owner invites the Members. **Do the Userpool Owner and Member related to the CLO-SET group's admin and users(collaborator, editor, viewer)?** No, the Userpool is a separate feature from CLO-SET group permissions.
content_description: Discover how to effectively manage your software licenses with Userpool in CLO Network Onlineauth 2024.2, enhancing security and collaboration by allowing authorized Members to access the Owner's license.

content: ### **Objective** In the 2D window, set an order between two selected Patterns to achieve stable simulation for a 3D Garment with multiple layers such as windbreaker, utilitarian jacket, and more. **Location ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![set_sublayer.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024684968) **Set Sublayer** ** Operation** 1. title: How to Create Bézier Curves
content: Create curves in CLO similarly to how they are drawn in Adobe Illustrator. Bézier curves are curves that are controlled and shaped by editing the handles that come with them. The resulting curves are CLO-internal. **※Note:** If a DXF is exported from CLO, Bézier curves are automatically converted to curves made out of Curve Points, a more common-across-software type of curve creation and control. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon** or **Internal Polygon/Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005618447/________.png) **Polygon** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670248/__________.png) **Internal Polygon/Line** ** Operation** **How to Create Bézier Curves** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon** or **Internal Polygon/Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005618447/________.png) **Polygon** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670248/__________.png) **Internal Polygon/Line** 2. Click and drag on the 2D window. The curve is created as the blue handles appear. → Continue to drag to adjust curvature. When the desired curvature is achieved, release your mouse button. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670268/__.png) 3. To draw a straight line or change the direction of the curve, click on the point created last. Then, continue to draw a shape with either the **Polygon** tool or a shape or line with **Internal Polygon/Line** tool. **How to Cancel/Reverse in-between** 1. To cancel all actions, hit the **Esc** key or **Ctrl+Z (Windows) / Cmmd+Z (Mac)** keys on the keyboard. → All the actions taken to create a shape with either the **Polygon** tool or a shape or line with the**Internal Polygon/Line** tool are undone. 2. To cancel the last step, hit the **Delete** or **Backspace** keys on the keyboard. → The point created last is undone.

title: Edit Curve Point
content: **List of Contents** **Add** **Edit** **Objective** Add and edit curve points on Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. ** ****Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Curve Point** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001096327/________.png) **Edit Curve Point** ** ****Operation** **Add** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Click the desired position of a segment to add a curve point. Or, Right click on a segment to split the segment by a curve point (ver 7.1) **Split into Two Lines** | Adjust by entering the length of both lines which are divided by the right clicked point, or by entering the ratio. ---|--- **Split by Length** | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. You can change the direction in which a point is added to a start/opposite/center basis. **Uniform Split** | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. → A free curve point is created at the selected point. → When a free curve point is added to an AI Bezier curve, the curvarture is changed based on the free curve point. **Move** 1. Click and drag a curve point or press the arrow key on the keyboard to move. To enter Moved Distance, right click while click-and-dragging the Curve Point **Distance Moved** | Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. ---|--- **X/ Y Axis** | Type in how much a point is moved on X/ Y-axis. title: Linked Editing
content: **List of Contents** **Setting** **Edit** **Options and Properties** ### **Objective ** You can quickly edit multiple patterns together by linking different pattern outlines. ### **Operation** **Setting** 1. Click the 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern (Z) tool. 2. Click one of the two segments to be edited simultaneously, or select multiple segments simultaneously while holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, and Right-click ▶ Link Lines menu. 3. Move the mouse cursor to click the opposite segment you want to edit simultaneously, or hold down the Shift key on your keyboard and click multiple segments. → Linked editing is set to both selected segments. **※ Note :** If the pattern has already been sewn, you can connect it more easily by right-clicking on the sewing line with the 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing(B) tool ▶ clicking the Link Lines menu. Even if it is not sewing, we recommend sewing first and setting Link Lines if necessary. **Edit** 1. Edit one side of the segment set for linked editing with 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern (Z) tool. → Based on the edited segment, the opposite segment is edited in the same direction in a symmetrical direction. **Options and Properties** 1. Click the 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Link tool. 2. Right-click on the segment set for linking and apply options as needed. **Unlink** | Remove the linked editing. ---|--- **Flip Direction** | Set to be simultaneously edited in the same direction. **※ Note:** You can also apply it in the property editor by clicking on the linked editing segment. **Add Sewing to Linking** | If there is no sewing line, a sewing line is added based on both lines set for linked editing.

title: How to Create Fur: Material Type "Fur (Render Only)"
content: #### **List of Contents** Apply Fur Fur Parameters Fur Gradation Color Fur Base Fur Maps (+ Fur Cluster Generator) Fur Gravity Fur Curl Fur Variance #### **Fur (Render Only) is a material type through which you can visualize realistic fur, fleece, etc. It can be applied onto any component in your 3D window or Object Browser that shows a Property Editor with a material type option. (E.g. fabrics, buttons, trims, avatars...) ** **This material type is render only, which means it can only be previewed during[Interactive Render](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render). If you wish to preview fur in the 3D window, check out material type [Fur Strand](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/44205065227801-Create-Fur-Strand-Beta).** **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/47286526797721)** #### #### **Apply Fur** 1. [Change the Material Type](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015998728-Material-Type) to **fur (render only)**. 2. If desired, select one of the presets to express fox, mink, angora, sherpa and more. #### #### **Fur Parameters** ** Option ** | ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- **Melanin** | Higher melanin value tints the color browner and darker. The lower the value, the more similar the color remains to the original color you set before. **Pheomelanin** | Higher pheomelanin value tints the fur redder. This value functions proportionally to the melanin value; the pheomelanin value is not taken into account when the melanin value is 0. **Glossiness** | Configure shininess of the fur. When light is shone onto the fur, a higher value makes it shinier. **Glossiness Boost** | Express coated fur. Glossiness adjusts intrinsic shininess of the fur whereas Glossiness Boost expresses the shininess from the fur finishing, like wax or coating. The higher the Glossiness Boost value is, the stronger the fur finishing effect appears. **Softness** | Express smoothness of the fur. Higher Softness value is makes the fur smoother. A lower makes it rougher. **Compensate Energy** | If light cannot pass through denser hair sufficiently, this compensates for a lack of light bounces throughout the affected area. #### #### **Fur Gradation Color** Click the check box to change any gradation properties. **Option** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Fur Gradation Color ** | ** Color ** | Select the mid and the tip color of the gradation. **Position** | Adjust the length of the fur where Mid and Tip Color is applied. ** Interpolation ** | Naturally blend the borders of tip, mid, and root colors. #### #### **Fur Base** ** Option** | ** Description ** ---|--- ** Length ** | Configure the length of the fur. A higher value corresponds to longer fur. Example: Length = **50 vs. 10** ![50.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033587) ![Untitled.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033607) ** Thickness ** | Configure the thickness of a single thread of the fur. A higher value corresponds to thicker strands. Example: Thickness = **10 vs. 0.20** ![Untitled_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956288) ![Untitled.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033607) **Bend** | Configure the bending strength of the fur. A higher value causes the strands to be more affected by gravity, therefore bending more. Example: Bend = **1 vs. 0.20** ![Untitled_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033807) ![Untitled_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033787) **Taper** | Differentiate the thickness of the fur between its root and the end. A higher value makes the strands become thinner towards their ends. A low value keeps a similar thickness between roots and ends. Example: Taper (with Thickness 2.00) = **1.00 vs. 0.00** ![Untitled_4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956388) ![Untitled_5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956448) **Density** | Configure how closely placed the strands are. Higher value corresponds to denser fur. Lower value gives a more scattered appearance. Example: Density = **1 vs. 0.20** ![50.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033587) ![Untitled_6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956468) **Segments** | Configure how many sections a single thread of fur is divided into. When the fur is long and has a higher bending value, the fur must have a higher amount of segments to express the Bending smoothly and realistically. However, for short and straight fur, this value is not as significant. #### #### **Fur Maps** Use base maps to express different levels of length, thickness, density, curl, bend, gravity, bend direction, and initial direction within a single pattern piece. **Maps for bend, length, thickness, density, curl, and gravity, like roughness and metalness maps, use a monochrome image as input** , with the image’s color values serving as the multiplier for the bend parameter. 0 is multiplied to the values when a map is black, while 1 is multiplied to the values when a map is white. **Maps for initial direction and bend direction define the direction of the fur and, like normal maps, use an RGB image as input** in red, green, and blue tones. The initial direction map determines the direction in which the fur initially grows, while the bend direction map defines how the fur curves from root to tip. _ Example: ![map_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360017402834) _ ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475777301017) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475800641817) You can easily generate the realistic Fur Cluster by controlling the length and bend direction. 1. 1. Open the **Fur Cluster Generator** by clicking the ![Inner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475777303833) button. 2. Generate the Fur Cluster. **Properties**** **| ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- ** Length ** ** ** ** ** | ** Cropping Map ** **** | Use the Cropping Map to apply different length within a single pattern piece. **Mode** | As a cropping map is grayscale, the length is determined based on the level of darkness (RGB) or the transparency (Alpha). Transparent and black areas have the lowest Length, while opaque and white areas have the highest Length. **Level** | Adjust intensity of gray tones. Increasing the value makes the cropping effect more obvious. **Low/High Length** | Adjust the shortest or longest fur length. ** Trimming ** ** ** | **Intensity** | Trim the length from the edge to the center of the fur cluster. Higher intensity increases the difference in fur length from the edge to the center to create a sharper fur. #### ![Fur Cluster_4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39510720113945) **Random** | Higher randomization makes the clumps irregular, while lower randomization makes the clumps consistent. ![Fur Cluster_5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40718701504025) ** Bend Direction ** **** | ** Cluster ** | **Intensity** | Adjusts the intensity of the fur bending in each direction. Higher intensity makes the fur clump more pronounced and dimensional. ![Fur Cluster_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39510720146713) **Pores Density** | Adjust the pores density of the fur cluster. Higher density makes the clumps smaller and tighter, while lower density makes the clumps larger and more spread out. ![Fur Cluster_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40153821981977) **Direction/****Intensity Random** | Adjust whether the bend direction is consistent or irregular. ** Detail Cluster ** | The clumping of smaller sub-units within the cluster can be adjusted in the same way as the cluster. **Relax** | Adjust the intensity of clumping in detail clusters while keeping each direction intact. Higher relaxation makes the clumps loosen smoothly, as if gently combed out. ![Fur Cluster_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39510741655705) #### #### **Fur Gravity** **Option** | ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- ** Force ** | Apply gravitational force. ** Vector ** | Manually apply a gravitational value to each axis. #### #### **Fur Curl** ** Option ** ** ** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Radius** | Configure the size of the curls. A higher value corresponds to larger curl and vice versa. Example (with Number 5.00): Radius = **5.00 vs. 1.00** ![Untitled_8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956808) ![Untitled_9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956828) **Number** | Configure the amount of curls. A higher value corresponds to more curls and vice versa. Example (with Radius 5.00): Number = **5.00 vs. 0.00** ![Untitled_8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956808) ![Untitled_9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956828) #### #### **Fur Variance** ** Option ** ** ** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Length** | Express uniform or irregular fur length. A higher value corresponds to more irregular fur length; lower value results in more uniform length variety. **Thickness** | Express uniform or irregular fur thickness. A higher value corresponds to more irregular fur thickness is; lower value results in more uniform thickness. **Direction** | Express uniform or irregular fur bending direction. A higher value corresponds to more irregular direction; lower value results in more uniform direction. **Gravity** | Express a uniform or irregular gravitational effect. A higher value causes a more irregular effect; lower value results in a more uniform effect. _A value can only be applied here if the Bending value is not 0._ #### **Back to List of Contents**
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide to the "Fur (Render Only)" material type, detailing its application, parameters, and customization options for creating realistic fur effects in 3D rendering.

title: Button/Buttonhole Pop-Up Menu
content: **List of Contents** Button/Buttonhole Pop-Up Menu Button Right Click Pop-Up Menu Buttonhole Right Click Pop-Up Menus **Button/Buttonhole Pop-Up Menu** \- Select desired options from the right-click pop-up menu to manage Buttons/Buttonholes. title: glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB) File
content: **List of Contents** Import Export Extensions **** Import or export glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB) files.![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947024654617) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/NHUPJ8ceaqs) **** #### **Import** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ **glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB)** 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. 3. Configure the settings and click **OK** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Open Type** | Open or add new files. **Object Type** | **Load as Avatar / Trim** | Load a GLTF/GLB file as an avatar / trim. **Arrangement Points** **Auto Generate** | It automatically creates a Bounding Volume/Arrangement Points suitable for GLTF/GLB. **Scale** | Type in the Scale or select the desired unit. * Commonly used default unit for GLTF file is Meter. **Axis Conversion** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. **** #### **Export** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ **glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB)** 2. Select the desired saving path and click **Save**. 3. Configure the settings and click **OK**. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Object** | **Select All Avatars/ Patterns/ Graphics/ Trims** | Select or deselect objects to be exported. **Single/ Multiple Objects** | Export the object as a single or multiple objects. **Unweld/Weld** | Choose to export vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects or a single point. **Thick/Thin** | Choose to export the object with the thickness or not. **Combined UV Coordinates** | A combined UV coordinates are also exported. **Option** | **Light** **(Except for Render Lights)** | Export along with lights **Garment Animation** | Export garment's animation. **Avatar Animation** | ## ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947024656537) Export Joint or Cached avatar animation. **Scale** | Select the unit or the size of the object. * Commonly used default unit for GLTF file is Meter. **Axis Conversion** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. **File** | **Save Colorway** | Choose whether you export colorway or not. Combine to One File/Multiple Files | Choose whether you combine all colorways into one file or create separate files for each colorway. **Save with glTF-Embedded (GLTF Only)** | Save textures as the glTF-Embedded format which includes texture files. **Save with Zip Files (ZIP)** **** | **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture** | When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting. **📝Note:** Since the color is diffused to the UV map when the Combined UV Coordinates is selected, the menu is hidden. **Exclude Ambient Map & Color (Modo)** | Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting.. **📝Note:** Since ambient maps and color are automatically excluded, the menu is hidden. **Save with MetaData (XML)** | Save garments' patterns (mesh), physical properties, and sewing information as MetaData (XML). **** #### **Extensions** **Property** | **Description** | **Required** ---|---|--- **Reflection Factor** | Reflection intensity of PBR material. In CLO, it has defaulted 15(0.15). Other engines and SW is defaulted 100(1.0) like the real world. | No, Default: 1.0

title: Project File (ZPRJ) Open/Add/Save
content: #### **List of Contents** **Open or Add** **Save** #### All information, including garments, avatars, 3D environments(background, lighting, wind, camera and simulation), animations, and so on, can be saved and loaded as one project file(ZPRJ). #### #### **Open or Add** 1. (Items that are not included will be disabled.) [**Colorway**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/32783140814105-Colorway) | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48730788207001) Choose specific colorways you want to open or add by clicking the ![Select Colorway.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48732648870041) **Select Colorway.**[**![Youtube Icon \(1\).png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/50834108001689)**](https://youtu.be/BxfRrxCtaXc?si=6Rb38Qvse-yv7d86)![Thumbnail=On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48732696469017) _* The thumbnail for each colorway shows the fabric that is most extensively used in that garment. However, the files created in 2025.1 or eariler will show only colorway names, without thumnails._ **📝Note:** When adding colorways, if you add more colorways than currently exist, the current colorway will be automatically duplicated to fill the gap. The items added this way (fabrics, graphics, trims, etc.) will be linked, so you can choose to unlink either only the materials or all properties. **Display Settings** | Select **Display Settings** to open the project file with the saved [3D and 2D display settings](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/29838353719321-Display-Setting-ver-2024-0). **📝 Note:** * If Display Settings is not selected, the display settings are reset to default. * When loading a previous file ver 2024.2 or before, Display Settings is deactivated. title: User Interface
content: You can customize the user interface settings. 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ **User Interface.** **** 2. Set up the user interface as needed. **Setting** | **Description** ---|--- **Unit** | **Unit System** | Set the default units (Millimeter, Centimeter, Inch) to be used in the program. **Decimal Places** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48729358555289) Set decimal places per unit (from 1 to 5) to make pattern editing more accurate. **Use Ligne (L) for Button Width** | Use the button size in L. **Default Topstitch Thread Thickness Unit** | Set the default unit for topstitch thickness. **Currency Unit** | Set the currency unit for [the Bill of Material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360045984074-Bill-of-Material). **Mode & Toolbar ** | **Default Mode** | Choose the default mode once you launch the application. **3D/2D/Render Toolbar** | Change the location of the 3D/2D/Render toolbar to the Top, Left, Right, or Bottom of the Render window. **Group Tools** | Group common tools to minimize the problem of some tools being hidden in the default layout. All manuals are written based on the tool grouping off state. **Show Manual and Video Links from Tooltips** | View or hide the manual and video links that appear in the tooltip. **Display** **(High-Resolution DPI Only)** | **Optimize for High Resolution** | By default, the interface magnification is optimized according to the display resolution. Change the resolution to QHD, FHD or 4K by turning off the option. When using multiple monitors, the high-resolution monitor must be set as the main monitor in the OS display settings. **Appearance** | **Line** | Customize the color of Pattern Outline, Internal line, Baseline, Selection, and Hover with thickness. Also, you can change the Line Length Size. **Highlight** | Change the color of the 3D Pattern Selection, Freeze/ Solidify/ Layer/ Bonding/ Solidify.

title: Nest Patterns
content: ### **List of Contents** Switch Mode Nest Pattern Nest Option Nest Settings Reset Default Arrangement Snapshot #### **Efficiently layout patterns and check fabric consumption to use the least amount of fabric.** **** #### #### **Switch Mode** 1. Switch to Print Layout mode on the top-right corner of CLO. #### #### **Nest Patterns** **All Fabrics** 1. Click the ![Nest Patterns All On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429417369)**Nest Pattern** tool in the toolbar. → Patterns are efficiently placed on the fabric and the calculated value is displayed. 2. Click the **Stop Nesting** tool in the toolbar. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** **Current Fabric** Selectively re-nest a specific fabric while preserving the results of other fabrics. 1. Click and hold ![Nest Patterns All On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429417369)**Nest All Fabrics** tool to switch to ![Nest Patterns On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429419417) **Nest Current Fabric** tool. → Only the selected fabric in Print Layout Editor will be nested. All other fabrics will remain unchanged. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** **📝****Note:** * Directly click the pattern ▶ Drag it within the set fabric width to place it or place the pattern using [Align](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000306628-Align) and [Distribute](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000295167-Distribute). * Instead of waiting for nesting to complete, stop directly at any point in time to place patterns to save nesting time. * The number of calculations varies depending on the number of patterns. Higher counts give optimal arrangement results, but larger numbers of patterns require more calculations and take more time. Moving one space of the progress bar means that once the calculation has been completed. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** #### **Nest Option** CLO automatically identifies the visual characteristics of textures and prints, and optimizes Nesting to ensure continuity with maximum efficiency. 1. Set how the pattern is matched by right-clicking on it in Print Layout mode or under Fabric in the pattern properties in Simulation mode. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Texture Based** | CLO automatically detects the texture placement on each pattern and nests them with optimal efficiency by ensuring texture alignment. The same arrangement is consistently applied across all sizes based on how the patterns are stacked. **Print Based** | Similar to the above Texture-Based Matching, but with the added Print. **Lock in Place** | Locks the Base Size placement in Print Layout as is, while the remaining patterns follow the Texture-Based concept. **📝****Note:** When Pattern Matching is set, the texture movement is restricted when using Edit Texture tool to prevent misalignment. However, the restriction on texture movement can be unlocked using the Pattern Matching Lock option under Fabric in the pattern properties in Simulation mode if needed. #### #### **Nest Settings** 1. Click the **Nest Setting** tool in the toolbar. → Nesting Options appear in the Property Editor. 2. Set each property. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Nesting** | **Number of Garment** | Nest grading patterns on the fabric for mass production. By clicking the Select Grading button, manually set the size and quantity(amount) of the grading patterns to be nested. **📝****Note:****** Different colors can be displayed for each grading size on the fabric and you can check the size names. ([**![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777)**](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)[ Watch Video](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)) • Display grading colors: 2D Pattern Display » Show Grading Random Color icon • Display grading names: 2D Information Display » Show Grading Size icon **Group Each Sizes** | Click the **Group Each Sizes** option to nest patterns by grouping the graded sizes separately. (**![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777)**[ Watch Video](https://youtu.be/JcJVKJlNuNw)) **Colorway** | Nest patterns of all colorways on the fabric or click Select Colorway on the right to place only the selected colorway on the fabric. **Grain Direction** | **1-way** | Place the pattern in one orientation along the original grain direction **2-way** | Place the pattern in the opposite orientation that is 180 degrees from the original orientation to achieve optimized results. **4-way** | Place the pattern in four different orientations that are each 90 degrees from the original orientation to achieve optimized results. **Buffer Spacing** | Set the spacing between patterns. **Pattern Dimension** | **Actual** | Place the pattern in its actual size. **Shrinkage** **/Growth** | Place the pattern with the shrinkage rate applied. **Information** | **Unit** | Set the units. **Fabric** | **Width** | Adjust the width of the fabric. **Length** | Check the total length of the fabric on which the pattern is placed. **Marker Length** | Set the length of the fabric manually to nest the pattern only up to the length of the set fabric. ([![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777) ](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)[Watch Video](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)) **Efficiency** | **Consumption** | Based on 100% of the total fabric, the fabric area consumed for the pattern is calculated as % **Remnant** | The remainder after subtracting the area consumed by the pattern is calculated as a %. **Area** | **Pattern Placed** | Check the pattern area placed on the fabric. **Remnant** | Check the remaining area where no pattern is placed. #### #### **Reset Default Arrangement** 1. Click the**Reset Default Arrangement** tool in the toolbar. → Patterns are reset to the initial arrangement state. #### #### **Snapshot** 1. Click the**Snapshot** tool in the toolbar. → 2D Snapshot pop-up window appears. 2. Set the size along with other options for the snapshot. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Size** | **Preset** | Select from a variety of presets. **Orientation** | Select the paper orientation. **Width** | Set the width of the image. **Height** | Set the height of the image. **Unit** | Set the unit of the print paper. **Resolution** | Set the resolution of the snapshot image. **Add'l Information** | Select the information that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Line Options** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48717971896857) Select the line that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Line Style** | Adjust the style of line in default Solid Line, Dotted Line, or Dashed Line. **Line Color** | Adjust the color of line. **Show Images** | Select the image that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Fabric Texture Opacity** | Adjust the opacity of the fabric and texture. **📝 Note:** Patterns and Internal Shapes with adhesion/bonding are classified separately in the **Bond** tab. #### Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for optimizing fabric layout and pattern nesting in CLO, ensuring efficient fabric consumption and arrangement.

title: Flatten
content: **Extract Patterns based on lines and shapes created on an Avatar.** **** **📝****Note:** * The Flattening function only extracts closed shapes as Patterns. * Since version 2024.2, the 2D pattern position and rotation are more aligned with the pattern placement on the 3D avatar. It is recommended to use CLO avatar for extracting the ideal pattern with front and back positions in the 2D window. When using a non-CLO avatar (eg. FBX) or missing the avatar, it is possible to lead to a non-ideal pattern position in the 2D window. #### 1. Click on the ![Flatten On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49948392732569)**Flatten** tool. → Points no longer appear and only lines appear on the Avatar. 2. Hover the mouse over the shape to be extracted as Pattern. 3. Select all areas to be extracted by holding Shift on the keyboard, then clicking on the desired areas. 4. Press**Enter** on the keyboard. → The selected areas on the Avatar are converted to patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. → Sewing lines are automatically established for adjacent Patterns. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49948555220761)** ## ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49948555225753) 5\. Hold down**Shift** and press **Enter**. → The intersecting area is flattened into a single pattern.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for extracting closed shape patterns from an Avatar using the Flattening tool, ensuring optimal alignment for 2D and 3D pattern placement.
